summary: Ahead of the US open the composite risk score sits at 42.47, unchanged on both the day and the week, holding a caution state inside a goldilocks regime. Overnight the rates complex moved in the risk-friendly direction: the 10Y yield eased to 4.63 from 4.7, the 2Y to 4.2 from 4.25 and the 10Y real rate to 2.4 from 2.43, while high-yield spreads tightened to 2.73 from 2.78. The offset is a hawkish policy headline, with a Fed governor signalling readiness to act on a rate hike to address inflation, and the VIX firming to 16.5 from 15.86 even as credit calmed. Beneath the surface the tape is unusually split: semis dispersion is extreme with Nvidia at 219.22 against AMD marked -7.0442, and not a single name in the breadth basket printed a new high despite 0.875 of it holding above its MA200. Model confidence is 0.7 and every feed except the calendar is flagged degraded, so read the level as directionally sound rather than precise.

top_risk_drivers.claim: Cross-asset confirmation is the single largest risk contributor at 0.5: equities, credit and crypto are only half aligned, so the pre-market calm rests on a narrow base rather than a broad consensus.
The 10Y real rate at 2.4 sits at the 98.25 percentile of its history and keeps macro the highest-scoring dimension at 75.26, even after the overnight easing.
The nominal 10Y yield at 4.63 remains a top-three contributor; it fell overnight from 4.7 but still prices at the 96.43 percentile of its range.
The VIX firmed to 16.5 from 15.86 while credit spreads tightened, a divergence that says hedging demand is being rebuilt into the open rather than unwound.
The new-highs ratio is 0.0 even though 0.875 of the breadth basket holds above its MA200 — leadership is being carried by a handful of names and is not confirmed by fresh highs.

supporting_signals.claim: Credit is the calmest block: high-yield spreads tightened to 2.73 from 2.78 and investment-grade held at 0.78, leaving liquidity and credit the lowest-scoring dimension at 14.13.
The curve stays positively sloped with 10Y over 2Y at 0.43, so the classic recession trigger is not firing even with the policy rate held at 3.63.
The trend block is intact: price sits 9.6661 above its MA200, 3-month momentum is 6.3584 and the 52-week drawdown is only -0.1997.
Market-implied inflation is not confirming the hawkish rhetoric: the 10Y breakeven eased to 2.22 from 2.23 overnight.

contradicting_signals.claim: A hawkish policy headline cuts against the overnight bond rally: the highest-ranked macro story in the feed, at importance 46.73, has a Fed governor saying she is prepared to act on a rate hike to address inflation.

Semiconductor dispersion is extreme rather than directional: AMD is marked -7.0442 while Nvidia is 3.4349 higher, yet the sector still shows 3.5789 of relative strength — index-level calm that hides single-name risk.

Risk appetite is narrowing at the edges: small caps trail the index by -0.2676 and Solana at 73.31 is lower on the session while Bitcoin at 64602.0 and Ether at 1902.7 hold gains, so the low-quality tail is not participating.

what_changed_today: Yields fell across the curve overnight: the 10Y to 4.63 from 4.7, the 2Y to 4.2 from 4.25, and the 10Y real rate to 2.4 from 2.43.
The VIX rose to 16.5 from 15.86, the only major risk gauge that deteriorated overnight.
High-yield spreads tightened to 2.73 from 2.78 while investment-grade was unchanged at 0.78.
The composite score is unchanged at 42.47 with both the 1-day and 1-week trend at 0.0, so the overnight moves offset each other rather than shifting the level.
A Fed governor publicly floated a rate hike to address inflation — the first hawkish escalation in the news feed and a direct counterweight to the softer yield prints.
watch_next: Whether the cash open sides with the bond rally or the hawkish Fed headline: with the 10Y at 4.63, a re-test back toward 4.7 would put macro pressure straight back on.
Whether the new-highs ratio can lift off 0.0; with 0.875 of the basket above its MA200 the raw material is there, but confirmation is missing.
Whether cross-asset confirmation improves from 0.5; a move higher would validate the goldilocks read, a move lower would make the caution state the operative one.
Whether semis dispersion narrows after the -7.0442 mark in AMD; another down session would challenge the 3.5789 sector relative strength that is currently holding the index up.
Data coverage: the calendar is empty for the next 7 days and every feed except the calendar is degraded, so the next clean macro print will move confidence more than usual.

bull_case.title: Credit and trend carry the tape through the open
points: Liquidity and credit score just 14.13 with high-yield at 2.73 — the funding channel shows no stress at all.
Price is 9.6661 above its MA200 with 3-month momentum at 6.3584; the primary uptrend has not been broken.
Falling nominal and real yields, 4.63 and 2.4, plus an easing breakeven at 2.22, give multiples room if the hawkish talk stays talk.

base_case.title: Range-bound caution with violent single-name dispersion
points: The score holds near 42.47 in a caution band; with the 1-day and 1-week trend both at 0.0 there is no momentum in the risk level itself.
Index-level volatility stays contained near a VIX of 16.5 while dispersion does the damage, as AMD at -7.0442 against Nvidia at 3.4349 already showed.
Macro stays the heavy dimension at 75.26 while credit at 14.13 offsets it, keeping the composite pinned rather than trending.

bear_case.title: Hawkish repricing meets a market with no new highs
points: If the rate-hike rhetoric gains traction, the 10Y at 4.63 re-tests 4.7 and a real rate above 2.4 compresses the multiple directly.
Breadth is fragile beneath the surface: a new-highs ratio of 0.0 and cross-asset confirmation of 0.5 mean there is no second line of support if leadership cracks.
The VIX is already rebuilding from 15.86 to 16.5 while spreads sit at tight levels of 2.73 and 0.78 — the asymmetry of a credit repricing is unfavourable.
